::: {.notes-block}
**Notes:**

<sup>1</sup> "Refinement" refers to allowing a change in mesh resolution for neighboring meshes.

<sup>2</sup> "Add/Remove" refers to the ability of the solver to handle changes in geometry during the course of the simulation, either by adding or removing `OBST` or `GEOM` via `CTRL` functions.

<sup>3</sup> "Velocity @ Mesh" refers to errors in the normal component of velocity at mesh boundaries, so-called "interpolated" boundaries in FDS. For inexact solvers, this error may be controlled using the parameter `VELOCITY_TOLERANCE`. Mass conservation errors are proportional to the velocity tolerance. Solvers listed as "exact" are *global* solvers. "Global" refers to a global matrix solution, one matrix for the whole domain, as opposed to one matrix per mesh. Thus, there are no mesh boundary errors for this type of solver.

<sup>4</sup> "Velocity @ Solid" refers to errors in the normal component of velocity at solid boundaries, so-called "penetration" errors that are present in *immersed boundary methods* and lead to mass conservation errors. These errors are particularly important to control for tightly sealed pressure zones. For inexact solvers, this error may be controlled using the parameter `VELOCITY_TOLERANCE`. Mass conservation errors are proportional to the velocity tolerance. Solvers listed as "exact" are *unstructured* solvers. "Unstructured" means the solid boundaries (e.g., `OBST` boundaries) are treated as domain boundaries for the pressure Poisson equation. Unstructured solvers are the opposite of *immersed boundary methods*.

<sup>5</sup> "Inseparability" refers to handling the error compared to the solution of the *inseparable* Poisson equation incurred by lagging the pressure in the baroclinic term. This error may be controlled using the parameter `PRESSURE_TOLERANCE`.

<sup>6</sup> Default ULMAT solver, recommended number of cells per mesh less than 150,000.

<sup>7</sup> ULMAT HYPRE and UGLMAT HYPRE use the HYPRE library developed at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratories (LLNL). Use this variant if the Intel MKL library is not available *or* if MKL runs out of memory or is too slow due to memory issues with large mesh blocks. Our implementation of HYPRE uses an algebraic multi-grid (AMG) preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) method, which does not require excessive amounts of memory.

<sup>8</sup> Default UGLMAT solver, addresses cases where the total number of cells is greater than 1 million.
:::

::: {.source}
FDS User's Guide, Table 21.1 (FDS-6.11.1).
:::

:::

::: {.notes}
- Table 21.1 of the FDS 6.11.1 User's Guide: what each solver allows and how it handles each kind of error.
- "Exact" means no error of that kind; "iterative" means it is reduced by pressure iterations down to VELOCITY_TOLERANCE. Unstructured solvers are exact at solids, global ones at mesh interfaces; only UGLMAT is exact at both.
- Inseparability is iterative for every solver (PRESSURE_TOLERANCE): why UGLMAT still iterated in the tunnel.
- Sizes from the notes: ULMAT PARDISO below ~150,000 cells per mesh; UGLMAT HYPRE, the UGLMAT default, above ~1 million cells in total; HYPRE wherever MKL is missing or runs out of memory.
:::

## Poisson Solver selection tips: {.selection-tips-slide}

::: {.slide-layout}

::: {.tbl .tips}
| Case | Characteristics | Poisson Solver Option |
|---|---|---|
| External flow, fire plumes, smoke transport in large open compartments | Relatively forgiving about mesh interface and solid boundary errors | Use default FFT.<br>If needed tighten velocity tolerance. |
| Internal flows, complex geometrical scenarios, many potentially sealed compartments | Possibly high mesh interface and solid penetration errors when using IBM. | Tighten velocity tolerance either with FFT or ULMAT. If problem/number of zones is small might consider UGLMAT. Large problem use UGLMAT HYPRE. |
| Long sealed domains, tunnels. | Possibly high pressure fluctuations with large pressure fields between single steps. | Use tunnel preconditioner (FFT, or ULMAT if internal obstacles present).<br>Can also try UGLMAT. |
:::

:::

::: {.notes}
- Fire plumes and large open spaces: the default FFT, as Example 4 showed; tighten (lower) VELOCITY_TOLERANCE if needed.
- Internal flows, complex geometry, sealed compartments: errors at solids matter (Examples 1–3). Tighten the tolerance with FFT or ULMAT, or use UGLMAT, with HYPRE for large problems.
- Long sealed domains, tunnels: the tunnel preconditioner with FFT, or ULMAT with internal obstacles, as in Example 5; UGLMAT also works, at a higher cost there.
- Whatever the choice, check the velocity error in the .out file and the mass or volume balance of your own case.
:::
